description: Alabama-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless a special hazard requires a lower speed, Alabama's maximum speed in an urban district is
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(1) says no person shall operate a vehicle in excess of 30 miles per hour in any urban district, except when a special hazard requires a lower speed to comply with section 32-5A-170.

questions.q: On an Alabama interstate highway, section 32-5A-171 sets the maximum at
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(4) says no person shall operate a motor vehicle on an interstate highway in Alabama at a speed in excess of 70 miles per hour unless a different maximum is authorized by the Governor under subdivision (6) or as provided in subdivision (7).

questions.q: On an Alabama highway with four or more traffic lanes that is not an interstate, the statutory maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(4) sets 65 miles per hour on any highway having four or more traffic lanes other than an interstate, unless the Governor authorizes a different maximum under subdivision (6) or as provided in subdivision (7).

questions.q: On Alabama highways other than interstates and other than highways with four or more lanes, the maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(3) sets 55 miles per hour on highways other than interstate highways or highways having four or more traffic lanes, unless a different maximum is authorized by the Governor under subdivision (6) or as provided in subdivision (7).

questions.q: Alabama's maximum on an unpaved county road, as defined in section 32-5A-171, is
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(2)a sets 35 miles per hour on any unpaved road. The statute defines an unpaved road as a county highway whose surface is natural earth, mixed or stabilized soil, aggregate, crushed sea shells, or similar material without asphalt, cement, or similar binders.

questions.q: On a county-maintained paved road in an unincorporated area of Alabama, the statutory maximum is
options: 30 mph because it is outside a city
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-171(2)b sets 45 miles per hour on a county-maintained paved road in an unincorporated area unless a different maximum is established under subdivision (6) or as provided in subdivision (7), subject to the maximum rate in subdivision (3).

questions.q: Alabama's per se rule for driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle is an alcohol level of
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-191(a)(1) says a person shall not drive or be in actual physical control of any vehicle while there is 0.08 percent or more by weight of alcohol in that person's blood. Impairment under (a)(2) through (a)(5) is a separate way to commit the offense.

questions.q: A person under 21 shall not drive or be in actual physical control of a vehicle in Alabama if the alcohol level is
options: Any reading only when a passenger is under 14
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-191(b) says a person under the age of 21 years shall not drive or be in actual physical control of any vehicle if there is 0.02 percent or more by weight of alcohol in that person's blood.

questions.q: On a first violation of Alabama's under-21 rule when the alcohol level is between 0.02 and 0.08, the license consequence stated in section 32-5A-191(b) is
options: A one-year revocation in every case
questions.explanation: Section 32-5A-191(b) says that on the first violation by a person whose blood alcohol level is between 0.02 and 0.08, the driver's license or driving privilege shall be suspended for 30 days in lieu of the penalties in subsection (e).

questions.q: For any Alabama license holder, ALEA's published point schedule produces a suspension when the driver has
questions.explanation: The ALEA Driver License Point System page says 12-14 points in a 2-year period is a 60-day suspension. Higher bands on that page are 15-17 points for 90 days, 18-20 for 120 days, 21-23 for 180 days, and 24 or more for 365 days.

questions.q: An Alabama Stage I learner's permit may be issued at age
questions.explanation: ALEA's Graduated Driver License page says a Stage I learner's permit requires the applicant to be age 15 or older. The holder may drive only when a parent, legal guardian, or licensed driver age 21 or older occupies the front seat, or when a licensed or certified driving instructor occupies that seat.

questions.q: Before an Alabama Stage II license, what practice or course proof does ALEA require of a student, in addition to the rule that a person under 18 must have held Stage I for at least 6 months?
options: A signed log of at least 50 practice hours, or proof of an approved driver education course
30 hours with 10 at night, and no course alternative
A road-skills score only, with neither practice hours nor a driver education course
questions.explanation: ALEA's Graduated Driver License page requires that student proof: at least 50 hours of behind-the-wheel practice on the ALEA verification form, or an SDE-approved driver education completion form. The same page says a person under 18 must have held a Stage I license for at least 6 months before Stage II, and needs permission from a parent, grandparent, or legal guardian.

questions.q: In Alabama, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Alabama requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver License | Alabama Law Enforcement Agency

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Alabama complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Alabama requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Section 32-6-7.2 Restrictions on Issuance to Persons Under 18 Years of Age

questions.q: In Alabama, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Alabama, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Alabama not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Alabama restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Alabama new drivers: off the road Midnight to 6 a.m..

provenance.manual: Section 32-6-7.2 Restrictions on Issuance to Persons Under 18 Years of Age

questions.q: In Alabama, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Alabama drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Alabama car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Alabama car knowledge test has 30 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Alabama car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Alabama car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Alabama, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Alabama, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Alabama, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: Section 32-5A-191 Driving While Under Influence of Alcohol, Controlled Substances, Etc.

questions.q: In Alabama, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Alabama sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Section 32-5A-191 Driving While Under Influence of Alcohol, Controlled Substances, Etc.

questions.q: In Alabama, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Alabama brings a suspension of 90 days.
questions.remember: Alabama, first refusal: 90 days without a license.

provenance.manual: Section 32-5-192 Implied Consent; When Tests Administered; Suspension of License or Permit to Drive, Etc., for Refusal to Submit to Test.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Alabama?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Alabama can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Alabama rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Alabama's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Alabama: only texting is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Section 32-5A-350.1 Operating a Motor Vehicle in a Distracted Manner; Violations; Exceptions.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Alabama?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Alabama, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Alabama left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Alabama's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Alabama seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Section 32-5B-4 Safety Belt Requirements for Occupants of Passenger Cars; Exemptions.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Alabama?
questions.explanation: Alabama requires a car seat or booster until 6 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Alabama: car or booster seat until 6 years.

provenance.manual: Child Restraints Law | Alabama Law Enforcement Agency

questions.q: What is Alabama's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Alabama requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Alabama's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Alabama can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.

provenance.manual: Driver License Point System | Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
